A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ferret-UI 2. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix reordering and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on elementary and advanced UI tasks, GUIDE, and GUI-World, plus cross-platform transfer and architecture/dataset ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports Ferret-UI 2 grounding results on ScreenSpot.

M1.justification: The architecture, adaptive N-gridding algorithm, training-data construction, and prompting procedure are unchanged. Appendix E's new pipeline illustration describes the predecessor Ferret-UI, not a new Ferret-UI 2 component.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds ScreenSpot evaluation across Mobile, Web, and Desktop. Desktop introduces an explicitly unseen platform beyond the five training platforms, materially extending evaluation coverage. Existing training datasets and earlier evaluation tasks are retained; Table 8 merely compares other datasets.

E2.justification: SeeClick becomes an evaluated comparator for the elementary/advanced tasks and GUIDE in Table 2 and GUI-World in Table 3. ScreenSpot additionally compares against CogAgent and SeeClick. Both were only cited in v1; these additions substantially strengthen independent GUI-specific comparisons.

E3.justification: The added ScreenSpot experiment reports grounding accuracy separately for Text and Icon/Widget categories across Mobile, Desktop, and Web, with an overall average. Existing evaluation metrics, model configurations, and ablation designs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a focused distribution-shift assessment: whether grounding transfers to new data on supported platforms and to the unsupported Desktop platform. The cross-platform and architecture/dataset ablations in Tables 4–5 and the qualitative inference examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experimental results. The added evaluations do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original scores remain unchanged, but substantial comparative results are added. SeeClick scores include 67.49 on advanced-task GPT-4o evaluation and 2.704 on GUI-World. New Table 7 reports ScreenSpot averages of 54.0% for Ferret-UI 2, 53.4% for SeeClick, and 47.4% for CogAgent, with new evidence of weaker Desktop transfer.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1, its distortion calculations, gridding constraint, and grid-count bound are unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about five-platform understanding, adaptive high-resolution encoding, improved training data, and cross-platform transfer. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix B introduces an applicability qualification: strong transfer to unseen data on supported Mobile/Web platforms accompanies weaker performance on the unseen Desktop platform. Earlier interpretations of the architecture/data ablations and cross-platform transfer remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that the added SeeClick comparison uses its original training data and QWen-VL-9.6B backbone, lists ScreenSpot comparator sizes, and supplies an exact 529,411-sample dataset total in Table 8. Existing preprocessing, prompts, resolution statistics, and label mapping are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix E and Table 8 explicitly compare dataset sizes, platforms, and tasks with earlier resources; Figure 6 illustrates the predecessor's data pipeline. Related-work categorization is lightly revised, while the bibliography and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, adds contact information and an ethics statement, and updates publication headers. The appendices gain ScreenSpot and dataset-comparison sections, while inference examples move from Appendix D to H. The main narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain comparator rows; v2 adds ScreenSpot and dataset-comparison tables and a predecessor-pipeline figure. Figure 1 corrects a widget tag, Figure 4 is reformatted, and existing appendix figures are resized or relocated. Their underlying examples and label statistics are retained.

improvement.justification: The SeeClick comparisons and external ScreenSpot evaluation strengthen empirical support while revealing a useful Desktop limitation. The dataset comparison also clarifies positioning. These gains are limited: ScreenSpot receives only brief protocol documentation, and the established method and principal results remain unchanged.
